# `fingerprint_band`

one band's features of a person over a span (MEG fingerprinting, steps 17 and 19), the region spectrum and the amplitude envelope correlation of its region signals.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run fingerprint_band --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run fingerprint_band --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run fingerprint_band --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest_alpha --map fp_A_alpha --lower 8 --upper 13 --from 5 --to 150
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording` | field recording, each true, where {"name": "$recording"} | yes |
| `map` | operator region map, from recording.manifold.0, where {"name": "$map"} | yes |
| `bad` | selection spans, manifold recording.time, where {"name": "{recording}_bad_segments"}, required false | no |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | `--recording` | `none` | - |  | the band's band-passed run, by name (`nxr-neuro run bandpass` of the run), or none: every recording of the subject, one run each |
| `map` | `--map` | `required` | - |  | the band's region map over the SAME span (`nxr-neuro run region_pca` of the band's kernel over this half) |
| `lower` | `--lower` | `required` | Hz |  | the band's lower edge: the second band-pass of the connectome, and the Hilbert transformer's length |
| `upper` | `--upper` | `required` | Hz |  | the band's upper edge (the second band-pass) |
| `name` | `--name` | `{map}` | - |  | the stem of the stored statistics: <name>_spectrum and <name>_aec |
| `single_bandpass` | `--single-bandpass` | false | - |  | false = the region signals are band-passed again before the Hilbert transform (the release's quirk: 2_preprocessing_AEC_ortho.m's process_aec1n) \| true = the Hilbert transform of the band-passed run's region signals as they are (the paper's reading) |
| `design` | `--design` | `brainstorm_2018` | - | brainstorm_2018, brainstorm | the second band-pass's filter: brainstorm_2018 (Brainstorm's release of 2018-10-12, the paper's: its transition bands, the ends padded with zeros) \| brainstorm (the current release's rule) |
| `beta` | `--beta` | `8.0` | - |  | the Hilbert transformer's Kaiser shape (8: a ripple of about 1e-4) |
| `segment_seconds` | `--segment-seconds` | `2.0` | s |  | the Welch segment's length (the release's win_length) |
| `segment_samples` | `--segment-samples` | none | samples |  | the segment's length in samples (wins over segment_seconds); null: from segment_seconds |
| `segment_rule` | `--segment-rule` | `round` | - | round, even, tile | how the segment's length becomes samples: round = round(seconds x fs) from the span's start (Brainstorm) \| even \| tile |
| `overlap` | `--overlap` | `0.5` | fraction |  | the fraction of a segment shared with the next (the release's win_overlap, 50 %) |
| `window` | `--window` | `hamming` | - | hann, hamming, blackman, rectangular | the taper of each segment (Brainstorm's bst_psd: Hamming) |
| `periodic` | `--periodic` | false | - |  | the DFT-even form of the window rather than the symmetric one (MATLAB's hamming(n), Brainstorm) |
| `detrend` | `--detrend` | `constant` | - | none, constant, linear | what is removed from each segment before windowing (Brainstorm: its mean) |
| `scaling` | `--scaling` | `brainstorm_2018` | - | brainstorm_2018, density, spectrum | brainstorm_2018 = \|2 X / n\|^2 at every bin (bst_psd of 2018-10-12, measure power: the release's units) \| density \| spectrum |
| `bad_segments` | `--bad-segments` | `exclude` | - | exclude, ignore | exclude = a segment touching one of the recording's bad segments is left out (Brainstorm) \| ignore |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chunks over `recording` | [`signal.linear_map`](../nodes.md) | x=recording, operator=map |  | regions |
| chunks over `recording` | [`signal.psd`](../nodes.md) | x=regions, exclude=bad | segment_seconds=$segment_seconds, segment_samples=$segment_samples, segment_rule=$segment_rule, overlap=$overlap, window=$window, periodic=$periodic, detrend=$detrend, scaling=$scaling, bad_segments=$bad_segments | spectrum |
| chunks over `recording` | [`signal.filter`](../nodes.md) | x=regions | kind=bandpass, lower=$lower, upper=$upper, design=$design, ends=span, remove_mean=false | banded |
| chunks over `recording` | [`signal.hilbert`](../nodes.md) | x=banded | lowest=$lower, beta=$beta, transform=envelope | envelope |
| chunks over `recording` | [`signal.hilbert`](../nodes.md) | x=regions | lowest=$lower, beta=$beta, transform=envelope | envelope |
| chunks over `recording` | [`stats.cov`](../nodes.md) | x=envelope | axis=region | covariance |
| after | [`stats.correlation`](../nodes.md) | covariance=covariance | measure=amplitude_envelope_correlation, warnings=["the band-pass and the Hilbert transform stream (chunks with halos): the envelopes differ from the 2018 release's whole-half filtering within about one filter length of each half's ends; measured on the synthetic goldens (compute/test/golden/gen_fingerprint_features_golden.m) the correlation differs by \|dr\| 6.6e-3 (delta, 1-4 Hz), 4.1e-4 (alpha, 8-13 Hz), 1.6e-5 (gamma, 30-50 Hz)"] | aec |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `spectrum` | kind statistic, name $name_spectrum, of recording, axes [{"name": "region"}, {"name": "frequency", "line": "{recording}_freq", "of_time": "recording.time"}], partition {"tiling": "$name_spectrum_segments", "on": "recording.time"} |
| `aec` | kind statistic, name $name_aec, of recording, axes [{"name": "region"}, {"name": "region"}] |

## Notes from the definition

```text
MEG BRAIN FINGERPRINTING, ONE BAND OF A PERSON OVER A SPAN (spec docs/specs/2026-11-16-meg-fingerprinting.md, section 11.3, steps 17 and 19, its amendment of 2026-11-19 and section 12: the published
method is the default, the release's quirks reproduced, the paper's reading a named option). The method: da Silva Castanheira J, Orozco Perez HD, Misic B, Baillet S (2021) Brief segments of
neurophysiological activity enable individual differentiation. Nat Commun 12:5713, doi:10.1038/s41467-021-25895-8; its authors' release megFingerprinting v1.0.0 (06fdba8), 2_prerprocessing_PSD.m and
2_preprocessing_AEC_ortho.m, with Brainstorm's release of 2018-10-12. Every stored result carries this citation (producer_json.references).

THE GRAPH (one run a band and a half: the recording is the band's band-passed run, the map the band's region map over the same half, the span the half):
  chunks:  signal.linear_map   the recording through the region map (a linear map, pointwise: one real series a region; the map's offsets are constants, removed below)  ->  regions
           signal.psd          step 17: Welch over the span, Brainstorm 2018's bst_psd: 2 s segments (round(2 fs), even) from the span's start, 50 % overlap, a symmetric Hamming window,
                               each segment's mean removed, |2 X / n|^2 at every bin (the release's power, no window correction), bad segments left out  ->  spectrum [regions x bins, 0.5 Hz]
           signal.filter       step 19: the region signals band-passed AGAIN (the release's quirk: process_aec1n's process_bandpass 'Compute' of 2018-10-12, its default filter), the SPAN being the
                               record: its ends padded with zeros, nothing outside it read; not with --single-bandpass (the paper's reading)  ->  banded
           signal.hilbert      the analytic signal (a FIR Hilbert transformer whose length follows the band's lower edge), transform envelope: its modulus |z|  ->  envelope
           stats.cov           the envelopes' covariance over the span (a statistic over the span's time partition, one block, its mean removed)  ->  covariance
  after:   stats.correlation   Pearson's correlation of every pair of regions (no orthogonalisation: the paper and the code agree)  ->  aec [regions x regions]
Stored: `<name>_spectrum` (power by welch, OF the recording; axes region x frequency, the frequency line of the segment length (the time line's fft operator row; an older `<recording>_freq` of the same grid is still found); its segments `<name>_spectrum_segments`) and `<name>_aec`
(measure amplitude_envelope_correlation by pearson, OF the recording; axes region x region). `run fingerprint_features` assembles the bands' into a person's two features.

It cannot resolve: what the region map cannot (a region's first principal component over THIS span, signed by a convention; neighbouring regions share signal through the beamformer's spread);
the spectrum is power per 0.5 Hz bin in the release's units (not a density); the envelope correlation of neighbouring regions is raised by that shared signal (no orthogonalisation, as the release);
the release computes the second band-pass and the Hilbert transform on the half held whole in memory (an FFT over it): here they stream, so the envelopes equal the release's away from the half's
ends and differ within about one filter length of them (the span's mean of the region signals, near zero for a band-passed signal, is not removed before the second band-pass).

  nxr-neuro run fingerprint_band --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest_alpha --map fp_A_alpha --lower 8 --upper 13 --from 5 --to 150
```
